title: If DC wants to beat Marvel at the box office, they need to stop being a follower and start acting like a leader

commenti.body:
I do think there's a definite point there: DC had been a duldrums all while Marvel was, at least commercially, reaping successes. DC only started working out when it started copying Marvel's approach (which, to put it succintly, is simply to churn out a string of action-farces) like Aquaman, Shazam...they're all done in that kind of camp, farcical style of a Marvel movie.

And now, with the hiring of James Gunn, who's credited with one of Marvel's biggest commercial successes and milestones, they clearly want the DC films to emulate that kind of overall style.

The issue is that not only does Gunn need to wash the stench of the old version of DC, get his new version off of the ground and get it a point of a consistent string of successes, he has to do it all while emulating Marvel and all while both Marvel and DC are faltering.

Personally, I think it'll all be too little, too late. The comics craze - which I deeply abhor by the way - is already starting to feel threadbare. Far be it from me to wish a filmmaker like Gunn to fail, but I do think these films are on their way out, and I think Hollywood will be better without them.

Yeah is anyone excited for The Marvels? I haven't watched anything past GOTG 3, but it looks like a grab bag of leftover characters that no one cares about. I don't think Brie Larson can carry the franchise on her back. It's not her fault, but Captain Marvel just isn't an interesting character at all.

Personally, I just don't care for those kinds of wimp films, honestly. I guess Iron Man and even The Avengers were still somewhat fresh. But the rest? I just don't need it. Give me more movies like Braveheart - serious, intense, gripping, cathartic - and less movies like Thor or Guardians of the Galaxy - light, knowingly-whacky, and wimpy.

They're basically Teletubbies for the big screen.
I get it. One of my favorite movies of all time is Payback. The right amount of funny and tough. To me it's a perfect film.

I didn't like The Flash for a lot of the reasons you mention.  The high speed saving the babies scene earlier is another example, felt like a lesser version of the Quicksilver scenes from the Xmen films.  Also had a lot of problems with likeability of their main character, that's outside of the actors problems.

It really comes down to needing to tell good stories, not just rehashes of every comic book story already told.  Sure you can get away with it, Batman still sells as does Superman, but they're at a point of diminishing returns.  Not going to get people out to lesser characters if it's the same old story even if they would for Batman.
